Package game.weather

Class MapGeography

java.lang.Object
game.weather.MapGeography
public class MapGeography extends Object
Places a game map on the real world, so that each tile has a latitude and a longitude.

The top-left tile sits at a chosen origin. Each step right adds a fixed number of degrees of longitude, and each step down takes away the same number of degrees of latitude, as on a real map where north is up. So the place asked about changes whenever an actor moves.

  • Constructor Details

    • MapGeography

      public MapGeography(double originLatitude, double originLongitude, double degreesPerTile)
      Places a map on the real world.
      Parameters:
      originLatitude - the latitude of the top-left tile, from -90 to 90
      originLongitude - the longitude of the top-left tile, from -180 to 180
      degreesPerTile - how many degrees one tile covers; must be positive
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the origin is not on Earth or the step is not positive

  • Method Details

    • latitudeOf

      public double latitudeOf(Location tile)
      Finds the latitude of a tile. Going down the map goes south; a result past a pole is cut back to the pole.
      Parameters:
      tile - the tile
      Returns:
      its latitude, from -90 to 90

    • longitudeOf

      public double longitudeOf(Location tile)
      Finds the longitude of a tile. Going right on the map goes east; a result past 180 wraps round to -180, as it does on Earth.
      Parameters:
      tile - the tile
      Returns:
      its longitude, from -180 up to but not including 180
